judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional definition of the Specifications; nothing elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.4 identifies the Specifications only by reference to an undated Project Manual, so the definition has no fixed referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A volume assembled for the Work which may include' bidding requirements and Conditions is permissive but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.3 leaves the Project Manual date as 'TBD' while 15.1.4 defines the Specifications by it, so the definition points to an unidentified volume.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Complementary, and what is required by one shall be as binding as if required by all' combined with performance 'reasonably inferable' from the Documents is a classic scope-of-work standard that parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 gives the Agreement precedence over inconsistent documents and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 imposes the more stringent requirement, so three different reconciliation rules coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short rule that specification organisation does not control trade division; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.2.1 and Agreement 10.1 on subcontracting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Words which have well-known technical or construction industry meanings' imports an undefined body of trade usage into the contract's vocabulary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on contested trade terms elsewhere, notably 'hand tools' in 7.5.1 and Exhibit C, but is not itself inconsistent with any provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capitalisation convention; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An interpretive rule about omitted modifiers and articles that itself tells courts to disregard textual differences — unusual, but clear in purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports harmonising the varied wording across the Agreement, Addendum and Supplementary Conditions; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the parties to sign the Contract Documents and provides for identification of unsigned ones; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Addendum and Supplementary Conditions bear blank execution dates and the Drawings and Specifications are unenumerated, so which documents were signed is not evident from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard site-visit representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Addendum 14.6(d) and must be read with A201 4.3.4's relief for unknown conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully drafted copyright and instruments-of-service provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Concerns the Architect's rights and does not interact with the payment or scope provisions; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text is fragmentary and the obligation (record legal title information within fifteen days of written request) can only be partly reconstructed from it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Relates to Agreement 4.1's provision for the Owner's time to file mortgages and mechanic's liens; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made' as a 'condition precedent to commencement or continuation of the Work' is an undefined sufficiency standard with drastic consequences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 14.1.1.4 lets the Contractor terminate for failure to furnish this evidence, and Addendum 6.5 gives the Owner a discretionary termination right, so the entry and exit conditions interact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates easements, assessments and charges to the Owner except permits and fees under 3.7.1; clear division.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees a reimbursable Cost of the Work, which softens the allocation but does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Owner furnishes surveys and legal description; Contractor may rely but must exercise care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2.1 and 4.3.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' and 'any other information or services relevant to the Contractor's performance ... under the Owner's control' are both open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 3 obliges the Owner to furnish and approve information 'in a timely manner', a slightly different standard for the same duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such copies ... as are reasonably necessary' is a modest standard in a minor provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.4 makes document reproduction a reimbursable cost, which overlaps the free-of-charge promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Persistently fails' is a soft trigger, but the remedy and its limits are clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2.4.1 (in both its A201 and Supplementary Conditions forms) and 12.2; the stop-work right is separate and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-stage seven-day notice procedure, spelled out in detail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.4.1 [Revision] replaces this with a single seven-day notice, so the instrument contains two incompatible versions of the same paragraph and c124's savings sentence leaves it unclear which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Contractor; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agreement's identification of Metzler Contracting Co. LLC.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence performance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Agreement Article 2 and its Addendum revision; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-relief provision; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.3 and 3.12.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires careful study and comparison yet says the obligations 'are not for the purpose of discovering errors, omissions, or inconsistencies' — a much-argued pair of sentences about how far a contractor must look.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for the correctness of measurements and bars extra charges for dimensional differences, which pulls in the opposite direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Distinguishes the Contractor's review 'as a contractor and not as a licensed design professional' while requiring prompt reporting of nonconformity; a workable but blurred line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 requires compliance with the more stringent code requirement, which assumes a degree of code review this clause disclaims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Liability turns on whether the Contractor 'recognized such error, inconsistency, omission or difference and knowingly failed to report it' — a knowledge test that generates disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b)'s no-extra-charge rule and 7.1.3.1's Change-Order-only limit on claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The warranty text is fragmentary in this copy and its exclusions ('improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage') are open-ended qualifiers on the core promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 conditions final payment on delivery and acceptance of all warranties, and A201 12.2.2/13.7 govern the correction and limitation periods.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Contractor to pay sales, consumer, use and similar taxes 'legally enacted when bids are received or negotiations concluded, whether or not yet effective'; the timing test is stated but fiddly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.2 makes such taxes a reimbursable Cost of the Work and Exhibit D expressly makes Hawaii general excise tax a job cost, so who bears the tax is answered two ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates the building permit and customarily-required fees to the Contractor; the 'customarily secured' qualifier is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.3 makes those same fees reimbursable and 2.2.2 assigns other assessments to the Owner, so payment and cost-bearing are split across documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short compliance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7.3-3.7.4 and 10.2.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Disclaims any duty to ascertain that the Documents comply with law while requiring notice of observed variances; the two halves sit in tension but are conventionally read together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 requires compliance with the more stringent of the Documents or applicable codes, which presupposes the comparison this clause disclaims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowing it to be contrary to laws' and 'appropriate responsibility' are judgment-laden but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 3.7.3 and 8.1.6's exclusion of costs due to the Contractor's failures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires allowances to be included in the Contract Sum with the Owner directing suppliers; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.4 leaves the allowances blank, so this machinery has nothing to operate on unless the Exhibits are treated as allowances.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed three-part allocation of what allowances cover and what stays in the Contract Sum; precise if intricate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With no allowances stated in 5.2.4, the adjustment mechanism is dormant, and it presupposes a fixed Contract Sum rather than cost-plus billing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In sufficient time to avoid delay' is an unquantified timing duty on the Owner.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with 8.3.1's delay extensions and 4.3.7's claim requirements; no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A competent superintendent and necessary assistants' with communications to him binding the Contractor; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum Article 2 [Revised] requires designation of one supervisory employee personally responsible for the project, and 10.2.6 requires a designated safety member — three overlapping designations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text is broken, but the duty (submit and keep current a schedule of submittals for the Architect's approval) is recognisable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4-3.10.5 govern the construction schedule in detail; the submittal schedule is a separate, consistent duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In general accordance with the most recent schedules' is a deliberately loose performance standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.10.4 makes the Construction Schedule a Contract Document requiring conformance, a stricter obligation than 'general accordance'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Record-copy and submittal-retention duties in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Agreement Article 11's records provision; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Shop Drawings; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Product Data; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Samples ... establish standards by which the Work will be judged' is definitional but does carry evidentiary weight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with 3.5's warranty and 12.2's correction obligations; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States clearly that submittals are not Contract Documents and explains their purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 declare schedules and cost estimates to be Contract Documents, so the categories drawn here are not observed elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Review-and-submit duties with 'reasonable promptness'; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.7 and 3.12.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation attaching to approval and submission; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2.1 field-measurement duties and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deviation exception requires specific written notice at the time of submittal plus approval or a Change Order; precise though demanding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 reinforces the Change Order requirement; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow procedural rule about resubmittals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.7; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and carefully qualified; 'unless the Contractor needs to provide such services in order to carry out ... construction means, methods' is the one movable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires shop drawings by a licensed engineer if the Architect, Owner or law requires, which shifts some design responsibility back to the Contractor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably encumber the site with materials or equipment' is a reasonableness standard, but a minor one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2.1 and 3.15 clean-up; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line responsibility for cutting, fitting and patching.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Extended to the Owner and separate contractors by 6.2.5; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably withhold' consent, twice, in a mutual formulation; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with 6.2.4-6.2.5; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned sentence is truncated ('access to the Work in preparation ... wherever lo'), so the extent of the access duty is not fully legible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Article 11's audit and access rights and 2.3/4.2.2 site visits; consistent in substance.
